product: HIV (Biktarvy, Descovy, Yeztugo and lenacapavir, new Bixlenvo), viral hepatitis (Livdelzi and seladelpar, bulevirtide), oncology (Trodelvy, Kite cell therapies Yescarta and Tecartus, and investigational anito-cel), plus declining COVID drug Veklury.
demand: Demand is solid in HIV, up 12 percent, and Trodelvy, up 26 percent, but shrinking in Cell Therapy, down 14 percent, and collapsing in Veklury, down 81 percent to 23M dollars. Gross profit is 7.80B dollars on 7.60B dollars of product sales in Q2 2026.
pricing_power: Pricing power is moderate and increasingly capped. US branded HIV and Trodelvy pricing holds, but low- and middle-income access via royalty-free voluntary licences and no-profit supply programs limits price, and competition constrains Trodelvy and CAR-T pricing.
competition: GSK and ViiV and Merck in long-acting HIV, J&J with Legend (Carvykti) and BMS (Abecma) in BCMA CAR-T, rival ADCs and chemotherapy in TNBC, and generic lenacapavir makers in emerging markets.
team: Led by Chairman and CEO Daniel O'Day, CFO Andrew Dickinson, Chief Commercial and Corporate Affairs Officer Johanna Mercier, and R&D leaders Dietmar Berger and Flavius Martin; Kite is the cell-therapy arm. Several executives sold shares in September 2026 under pre-set 10b5-1 plans.
market_strategy: Fund a 32B dollar US investment through 2030 and about 3,000 domestic jobs, expand oncology through the Arcellx, Tubulis and Ouro Medicines deals, and defend HIV leadership by converting lenacapavir into oral and long-acting PrEP and treatment while widening global access through licensing and PAHO.
bull: Q2 2026 revenue $7.8B, +10.6%, driven by volume: HIV +12% to $5.7B, Trodelvy +26%; Bixlenvo approved 2026-08-27 and anito-cel PDUFA 2026-12-23 are dated catalysts.
bear: Q2 2026 GAAP loss $8.45/share on $11.2B acquired IPR&D; cash fell to $3.2B from $10.6B; Cell Therapy -14%, Veklury -81%; net analyst target changes -3 over 90d; insiders sold in September 2026.
falsifier: Q3 2026 earnings on 2026-10-29 showing HIV growth below 12% or further cash decline below $3.2B would prove the bull case wrong.
web_what_changed: FDA approved Bixlenvo bictegravir plus lenacapavir single tablet regimen on 2026-08-27 after an 08-27-2026 PDUFA. EC authorized Trodelvy plus Keytruda in PD-L1-positive TNBC on 2026-08-24. Q2 2026 results (reported 2026-08-03/04) showed revenue 7.8B dollars up 10.6 percent but an 8.45 dollar GAAP loss on 11.2B dollars of acquired IPR&D from Arcellx, Tubulis and Ouro Medicines.
web_not_known_yesterday: No new material disclosure dated 2026-09-24 or 2026-09-25 found. The most recent items are insider-form filings: SVP Controllership Erin Burkhart converted 2,223 RSUs on 2026-09-22, and CFO Andrew Dickinson sold 3,000 shares on 2026-09-15 under a Rule 10b5-1 plan. Bixlenvo approval has been known since 2026-08-27. Status: not found for same-day news.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Growth is volume and mix, not price. Q2 2026 HIV rose 12 percent to 5.7B dollars on Biktarvy plus 7 percent and Descovy plus 48 percent; Trodelvy plus 26 percent to 457M dollars; Livdelzi grew. Cell Therapy fell 14 percent to 417M dollars and Veklury fell 81 percent to 23M dollars. No price-driven breakout was disclosed.
web_suppliers: Gilead largely self-manufactures and does not disclose a concentrated supplier list; no supplier constraint was found. Lenacapavir for low-income countries is licensed royalty-free to Dr. Reddy's, Emcure, Eva Pharma, Ferozsons, Hetero and Mylan for manufacturing readiness and technology transfer during PURPOSE 365. Cell Therapy output fell 14 percent, suggesting internal rather than supply constraint.
web_customers: Not found precisely. Gilead sells through US specialty distributors and wholesalers and to government and multilateral buyers (PEPFAR, Global Fund, PAHO Regional Revolving Funds for 14 Latin America and Caribbean states). LMIC volumes flow via voluntary licensees. No numeric customer-concentration disclosure was read; wholesale concentration is historically high.
web_who_loses: HIV rivals lose if long-acting lenacapavir wins: GSK and ViiV (dolutegravir and cabotegravir), Merck (islatravir) and daily oral regimens. In myeloma CAR-T, J&J with Legend (Carvykti) and BMS (Abecma) lose if anito-cel launches after 2026-12-23. In TNBC, generic chemotherapy and rival ADCs lose; generic lenacapavir makers cede branded share in rich markets.
web_contradicting_evidence: Q2 2026 non-GAAP loss was 6.75 dollars per share and GAAP net income was negative, giving a negative P/E. Cash fell to 3.2B dollars from 10.6B dollars after 11.3B dollars of acquisition outflows; debt-to-equity 2.03; dividend payout ratio negative. Leerink downgraded to Market Perform and cut target 146 to 127 dollars on 2026-07-21; Barclays cut to 145 dollars on 2026-07-29. Insiders sold: CEO 15,000 shares in September 2026.
web_if_management_right: Lenacapavir becomes an HIV backbone (Bixlenvo orally, Yeztugo as twice-yearly PrEP), lifting HIV well above 12 percent growth; anito-cel launches after the 2026-12-23 PDUFA and becomes a foundational myeloma therapy including earlier lines; FY2026 product sales reach 30.1 to 30.4B dollars; oncology and inflammation scale; adjusted EPS turns positive in 2027.
web_if_management_wrong: HIV franchise erodes first if long-acting competition and payer pressure bite and if the lenacapavir franchise cannibalizes Biktarvy without net growth. Then the balance sheet breaks: 3.2B dollars of cash, high acquisition debt and IPR&D charges block buybacks and threaten the dividend, while anito-cel CAR-T economics and Cell Therapy decline leave oncology unable to offset Veklury's disappearance.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Contract manufacturers and CDMOs making lenacapavir and its long-acting formulation; the royalty-free licensees Dr. Reddy's, Emcure, Eva Pharma, Ferozsons, Hetero and Mylan; PEPFAR, Global Fund and PAHO procurement channels; Kite cell-therapy logistics and apheresis partners; and ADC supply-chain and conjugation vendors for Trodelvy.
